scope: How future AI work finds its owner, limits context, validates changes and reverses decisions.

sources_of_truth.actual_implementation: Source code and executable checks when created; contracts describe required behavior, not implemented status.

implemented_checks: Strict JSON parsing and required design-record shapes
Route owners, scenario links and decision links
Synthetic source locators, quoted evidence and expected-claim references
design_validation.limits: These checks validate design consistency and fixture integrity. They do not inspect product imports, execute a parser or model, prove semantic support, or demonstrate persistence/authority enforcement; G01-G05 and the remaining G06 work still require implementation.

context_protocol: Read the entry contract and choose a change route; determine whether the request changes behavior, interpretation, data, presentation or authority.
Read the owner module, its public contracts and relevant decisions. Read immediate consumers only if their contract or observable behavior may change.
Build a small change record with goal, affected owners/contracts, acceptance evidence and rollback method; a normal issue or PR body is sufficient for ordinary work.
If no route fits, add a specific owner or amend an existing boundary with rationale before implementing. Do not place new behavior in a global utils/service bucket.
Expand context when evidence reveals impact; do not silently assume an unfamiliar dependency is irrelevant.

Update affected contracts in the same change when public behavior, ownership, authority or compatibility changes. A private implementation change does not require rewriting unchanged design contracts. Generate inventories from code where possible instead of maintaining duplicate summaries.

change_routes.trigger: Change navigation, map layout, visual grouping or desktop framework
change_routes.rollback: Switch the renderer/view implementation; no domain-data migration should be required.

change_routes.trigger: Add or replace a source-language parser
must_preserve: Observation schema or explicit version migration
change_routes.rollback: Select previous analyzer; invalidate only version-dependent derived outputs.

change_routes.trigger: Change coupling heuristics, business-module extraction or AI prompts
change_routes.rollback: Select previous analysis version and rebuild projections; preserve adopted output snapshots.

change_routes.trigger: Replace model/provider or change fast/deep routing
change_routes.rollback: Restore prior configured adapter/profile if authorized and available; otherwise expose degraded state.

change_routes.trigger: Attach an idea to an analysis entity or adopt an evidence-backed explanation
must_preserve: Exact adopted output and permitted evidence
Atomic owner revision and command completion
change_routes.rollback: Supersede owner intent through a new revision; failed transactions publish no adoption and unreferenced artifacts are collected.

change_routes.trigger: Revise, withdraw or branch an idea or desired module boundary
change_routes.rollback: Create a superseding revision; flag dependent plans for review without erasing history.

change_routes.trigger: Change prioritization, task decomposition or acceptance criteria
change_routes.rollback: Publish a new plan revision based on an earlier one; never reuse old evidence as proof of changed criteria.

change_routes.trigger: Add CI, release or runtime-health evidence
change_routes.rollback: Disable adapter; keep prior observations visibly historical.

change_routes.trigger: Change the persistence engine or shared artifact/export container

owner_selection.rule: Include owners whose actual store, transaction or compatibility contract changes. A shared engine replacement may affect all persisted owners; establish that impact instead of reading every module by default.

change_routes.rollback: Use compatible schema rollback, tested forward repair or explicit restore; do not claim destructive data migrations are automatically reversible.

change_routes.trigger: Change a module's retained record semantics, schema, export mapping or retention

owner_selection.rule: The affected data owners define compatibility and migrations. Add adapters for serialization/engine changes and application for changed multi-owner transaction behavior.

change_routes.inspect_rule: Read affected public consumers and shared transaction/artifact contracts only when changed.
change_routes.rollback: Use an owner-reviewed compatibility reader, forward repair or verified restore with later edits accounted for.

change_routes.trigger: Enable code changes, commands or deployment
change_routes.rollback: Stop new dispatch, reconcile in-flight outcomes and compensate where supported; local rollback cannot reverse remote effects.

change_routes.trigger: Add a desktop OS or WSL collector
change_routes.rollback: Disable new host/transport and retain the canonical store; leave source registration reconnectable.

change_routes.trigger: Split, merge or rewrite a module because the current boundary is wrong

owner_selection.rule: Select current and destination owners for transferred behavior/data. Include application only if orchestration changes; it does not inherit domain ownership.

change_routes.inspect_rule: Start with changed contracts and their immediate consumers; expand only when dependency or migration evidence shows impact.
change_routes.rollback: Use a temporary compatibility adapter, single active writer and migration checkpoint; retire the old path after the defined observation window.

replacement_protocol: Identify the observable behavior and data ownership to preserve; record what intentionally changes.
Create boundary-level fixtures from representative allowed inputs, including unknown, error and partial cases.
Implement the replacement behind the existing port or a versioned successor. Keep one active canonical writer.
Compare old and new outputs read-only on the same fixtures. Normalize unstable ordering; assess semantic and coverage differences explicitly.
Switch a bounded path to the new implementation and observe errors, latency, data integrity and owner comprehension.
Retain a compatible rollback path for a defined interval, then remove the old implementation and temporary routing. Do not keep perpetual dual implementations.

reversal_types.mechanism: Superseding revision plus dependent-plan review; preserve history.
Invalidate/rebuild by input and analyzer version; preserve exact adopted results.
Switch compatible implementation behind a tested boundary.
Compatibility reader, forward repair or verified restore with post-backup edits accounted for.
Outcome reconciliation and operation-specific compensation; no generic undo promise.

boundary_review_triggers: The same feature repeatedly requires private changes across several owners.
Application orchestration accumulates rules that belong to a domain owner.
A shared type gains unrelated fields for unrelated consumers.
A module cannot be tested without booting UI, AI or unrelated modules.
Replacing a provider or renderer forces canonical owner-data changes.
A large DTO or global graph requires every agent to understand the whole product.

architecture_gates.name: Dependency boundaries
architecture_gates.check: Compare actual project/namespace references with module allowlists; reject cycles, private cross-module imports and domain framework dependencies.

architecture_gates.name: Boundary schemas
architecture_gates.check: Validate versioned AI, collector and export records; reject unknown evidence references and unsupported versions. Internal types use compiler checks.

architecture_gates.name: Behavior and provenance
architecture_gates.check: Run affected acceptance fixtures, including unknown/partial/stale states and source revision identity. For interpretation changes, review factual correctness, semantic evidence support and explicit unknowns; passing an output schema is insufficient.

architecture_gates.name: Persistence compatibility
architecture_gates.check: Restore a fresh profile, migrate supported stored fixtures, verify pinned artifacts and reject incompatible writers.

architecture_gates.name: Authority enforcement
architecture_gates.check: Before collection, verify allowed roots, excluded data and untrusted content handling. Add denied-provider, concurrent-budget and execution-scope checks before the corresponding integration.

architecture_gates.name: Context and decision drift
architecture_gates.check: Local design references, declared ownership and dependency graph are checked. Source/contract drift enforcement and human rationale review remain required when product code exists.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Owner notes are attached to stable module references
acceptance_scenarios.when: A map is regrouped or a desired structure is edited
acceptance_scenarios.then: Notes remain attached or explicitly unresolved; observed source relationships are unchanged.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Owner decisions reference retained evidence and a derived map exists
acceptance_scenarios.when: All disposable indexes are removed and rebuilt
acceptance_scenarios.then: Owner IDs, revisions, pinned evidence and adopted explanations survive; only projections regenerate.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Two analyses use different source generations
acceptance_scenarios.when: The older job finishes last or omits evidence
acceptance_scenarios.then: It cannot replace the newer current view; unsupported claims are rejected or shown as inference/unknown.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An AI provider is unavailable or replaced
acceptance_scenarios.when: The owner browses existing work and starts new analysis
acceptance_scenarios.then: Stored work remains usable, pending work is honest, and no unauthorized fallback receives source content.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A decision produced a plan with verification history
acceptance_scenarios.when: The owner withdraws the decision or changes acceptance criteria
acceptance_scenarios.then: History is retained and dependent work is flagged; old verification does not prove the new criteria.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Tests pass locally without deployment or telemetry evidence
acceptance_scenarios.then: Implementation, validation, release and health remain separate; missing release/health evidence is unknown.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Collection or publication is in progress
acceptance_scenarios.when: The host/collector crashes, files move or events are missed
acceptance_scenarios.then: Restart reconciles without duplicate adopted records, stale overwrite or silent note reassignment; ambiguous identities stay unresolved.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A representative sized graph and active background analysis
acceptance_scenarios.when: The owner navigates, cancels work and explores a focused module
acceptance_scenarios.then: The UI meets measured responsiveness targets, has keyboard/list alternatives and reports the displayed data generation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Source contains malicious instructions, escaping paths or restricted content
acceptance_scenarios.when: A scanner/model/collector processes it or concurrent paid requests are scheduled
acceptance_scenarios.then: Authority cannot expand, excluded data stays excluded, budgets are enforced and secrets are absent from output/logs.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A populated profile with user edits and retained artifacts
acceptance_scenarios.when: It is exported/restored, migrated or opened by an incompatible older writer
acceptance_scenarios.then: Supported restores preserve references and hashes; incompatible writes are refused; backup cutoffs and possible later edits are explicit.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An external execution request times out after possible dispatch
acceptance_scenarios.then: The outcome is reconciled before retrying a non-idempotent action; a local revert is not reported as remote undo.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A module has a candidate replacement
acceptance_scenarios.when: Both run read-only against identical fixtures and the active implementation is switched
acceptance_scenarios.then: Boundary behavior is compared, one writer remains active, data migration is explicit and rollback behavior is demonstrated.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Reviewed source examples with supported facts, likely capabilities and intentionally unavailable information
acceptance_scenarios.when: A parser, prompt or provider produces an explanation
acceptance_scenarios.then: Required facts and evidence are correct, capability meaning stays an interpretation, dynamic targets and runtime status remain unknown when unsupported, and no forbidden conclusion is asserted.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An exact analysis output and permitted source artifacts are ready for adoption
acceptance_scenarios.when: Adoption succeeds, conflicts, loses required input, crashes or is retried
acceptance_scenarios.then: Output, evidence pins, owner decision and command completion commit together or not at all; retries do not duplicate records and orphan artifacts cannot appear as a successful adoption.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An owner note references a source or interpreted entity
acceptance_scenarios.when: Analysis is replaced, disposable indexes are deleted, or the entity splits or merges
acceptance_scenarios.then: The original anchor and note survive. Supported continuity may retain identity; ambiguous mappings remain explicitly unresolved until a revisioned owner association, without silent note reassignment.

validation_sequence.deliverable: These contracts, local design checker, reviewed synthetic quality expectations, change routes and decision rationale.
validation_sequence.exit: The design checker and its regression tests pass. References, declared dependencies and scenario routing are checked; no runtime capability or explanation quality pass is claimed.

validation_sequence.deliverable: Minimal headless slice: repository snapshot, one supported analyzer, evidence query and revisioned idea persistence, plus a bounded desktop packaging/graph performance spike.
validation_sequence.exit: G01/G02/G06 exist; S01/S02/S03/S07/S10 pass for implemented scope. Confirm first source language, target OS and measured graph limits before committing to broad features.

validation_sequence.deliverable: Focused desktop map, evidence drill-down, ideas, retained adoption, fresh/stale status and fast/deep inference ports.
validation_sequence.exit: The first-delivery success checks pass against reviewed synthetic and selected real-repository examples; the owner can explain capabilities and uncertainty. AI/provider permissions are explicit; S04/S08/S09/S13/S14/S15 pass for applicable implemented scope.

validation_sequence.deliverable: Revisioned scenarios, plans, task handoff and criterion-linked results.
validation_sequence.exit: S05/S06 pass; changing a decision visibly invalidates dependent assumptions without deleting history.

validation_sequence.deliverable: Additional languages, repositories, runtime evidence or explicitly authorized execution, selected by demonstrated need.
validation_sequence.exit: Each adapter passes its boundary fixtures and applicable authority/recovery scenarios; no automatic all-language or all-platform claim.

acceptance_application.scope: Record the implemented slice, applicable scenario cases, deferred integrations and evidence at a specific revision. A deferred or unexecuted case is not a pass, and synthetic examples do not replace final reference-repository acceptance.
acceptance_application.quality_review: Check required facts and forbidden conclusions, then review whether cited evidence actually supports capability interpretations. Allow equivalent plain-Chinese wording and differing valid groupings; do not require exact AI prose or graph layouts.
acceptance_application.experiment_exit: Before a bounded packaging, graph or analyzer prototype, record the question, relevant environment, acceptance evidence and stop condition. Confirm measured limits before broadening scope; retire temporary code and fixtures that no longer serve a retained behavior.

open_inputs_policy: Target OS, reference repository, language scope, data permission and spending limits remain user/environment inputs. They do not block architecture or local deterministic fixtures; they block only dependent integrations and final acceptance targets.
